articles.author: Catherine Osborn
articles.description: Brazil's 80-year-old left-wing leader President Lula defeats Flávio Bolsonaro in a bitterly contested runoff.
articles.title: Brazil's left-wing President Lula elected for fourth term

articles.author: Chandelis Duster
articles.description: Pennsylvania is the worst hit state, with at least 1,338 cases of measles confirmed in 44 counties so far this year, according to the Pennsylvania Department of Health.
articles.title: U.S. measles cases more than double what they were last year as outbreak spreads

articles.author: Willem Marx
articles.description: Attorney General Todd Blanche defended the Justice Department's suit over Alaska's Senate race in an interview on CNN.
articles.title: Blanche defends DOJ lawsuit blocking Alaska Senate results if Republican loses

articles.author: Carrie Kahn
articles.description: Machado announced her arrival on social media, writing "I am here. With you."
articles.title: Venezuela's opposition leader María Corina Machado returns after months in exile

articles.author: Daniel Estrin
articles.description: Israel is holding a general election this week after years of war. For many Israelis, shaken by the Oct. 7, 2023, attacks and years of war, it is the most consequential in decades.
articles.title: Israelis have changed. Will they change their leadership?

articles.author: Julie Bourdin
articles.description: The students, many from marginalized communities, learn to conjure up candy, do card tricks — and face the world with a confident, creative and resilient mindset.
articles.title: This College of Magic turns ordinary kids into cool magicians

articles.author: Samantha Balaban
articles.description: Every fall, snow geese migrating south stop in Vermont and cover the ground in a snowy white blanket. Now, a new picture book celebrates that real-life awe-inspiring event.
articles.title: In this new kids' book, it's 'Snow Geese Season' for a little boy and his Pop

articles.author: Chloe Veltman
articles.description: The recent Meta settlement includes a clause banning "cosmetic procedure filters" for teens. But defining what constitutes an extreme makeover isn't easy.
articles.title: When a teen posts a selfie, how much filter is 'too much' filter?

articles.author: Elly Yu
articles.description: The U.S. has no national law for paid parental leave. But in states that do, more dads are using the benefit, sometimes more than moms. The change comes as Americans say having kids is unaffordable.
articles.title: More dads taking paid family leave for a new baby, sometimes as much as moms are

articles.author: Barbara Sprunt
articles.description: As they look to win the Senate, Democrats are hoping that independent candidates in Nebraska and Montana can help them topple Republicans in a part of the country where their own brand is hurting.
articles.title: Independent candidates sense a moment. Some Democrats hope they're right.

articles.author: Kat Wong
articles.description:
Follow live updates

Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Steggall calls for civility and respect
Independent MP Zali Steggall has called for more respect in times of disagreement, telling ABC that leadership and words matter.
We absolutely need to make sure there is more civility and respect.
Social media is a platform where they can send abuse and threats through direct messages, call my electorate office, or send pretty revolting stuff
It’s just quite shocking how disconnected from manners and reality sometimes people get when they launch into their diatribes and make threats.
There’s been a lot of money and a lot of effort and a lot of thought going into security here at Parliament House.
I think the vulnerability is actually when we’re out doing our job in the community, and that’s probably where we need to put the focus.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Australia politics live: Haines’s first words after waking were of concern for staff and bystanders; restrained start to question time

articles.author: Adam Fulton (now); Marina Dunbar (earlier)
articles.description:
Leftist president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva defeated the far-right senator and was elected president of Brazil for a fourth non-consecutive term

Full report: Lula wins fourth term as Brazil’s president over Flávio Bolsonaro

Live second round results

The local electoral court ordered the immediate restoration of 100% of the bus fleet and ordered the arrest of the municipal transport secretary, Pablo Souza, on suspicion of an electoral offence and disobeying court orders. The arrest warrant could not be carried out, however, because he is in Paris on what the city government described as an “official mission”, and is not expected to return to Brazil until Monday.
Late in the afternoon, Flávio Bolsonaro also filed requests for voting to be extended by two hours in cities in the states of São Paulo, Paraná and Santa Catarina, but because of heavy rain that he said had prevented voters from turning out.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Brazil runoff live updates: Bolsonaro says it is ‘impossible to concede’ election result after historic Lula win

articles.author: Jordyn Beazley
articles.description:
Former police officer accused of shooting dead Jesse Baird and Luke Davies apologised to friend, acknowledging ‘you’re involved because of me’

Follow our Australia politics live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A covert recording captured Beau Lamarre-Condon telling a friend during a meeting in prison in December last year, “I fully take accountability that you’re involved because of me now,” a Sydney court has heard.
Lamarre-Condon, 31, is accused of fatally shooting couple Jesse Baird and Luke Davies with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home on 19 February 2024.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Covert recording of prison meeting between Beau Lamarre-Condon and friend played to double murder trial

articles.author: Benita Kolovos Victorian state correspondent
articles.description:
Paul Edbrooke says he fears for family’s safety amid heightened concerns for MPs after alleged attack on Helen Haines

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Victoria’s emergency services minister believes he is being followed and fears for his family’s safety after a bullet, etched with the word “RAT” and his former firefighter number, was left on his car.
The Herald Sun first reported on Monday that Paul Edbrooke had returned to his car after a community event in his Frankston electorate on Saturday and found the bullet on the bonnet. He later told reporters he had only been away from the car for about an hour and made the “chilling” discovery on his return.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Someone has been following me’: safety fears after bullet inscribed with ‘RAT’ left on Victorian minister’s car

articles.author: Australian Associated Press
articles.description:
Prohibition of salty, yeast-based condiment in Victoria’s prisons remains after convicted murderer claimed it denied him right to ‘enjoy his culture’

Follow our Australia politics live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A murderer who claimed a refusal to allow him Vegemite in prison is a breach of his human rights as an Australian has failed to overturn the ban on the polarising spread.
Andre McKechnie sued Victoria’s corrections department after he was refused the salty, yeast-based condiment in prison.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: There’s no human right to Vegemite, court tells Australian prisoner who wanted ban overturned

articles.author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
articles.description:
Allegra Spender calls Indi MP ‘force for change’ as politicians pay tribute in parliament  

Follow our Australian politics live blog for latest updates

Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Helen Haines’s first words after an alleged attack last week were to ask about the safety of her staff and express gratitude to bystanders and doctors.
Allegra Spender, the MP for Wentworth, told parliament on Monday that Haines’s husband, Phil Haines, had revealed the Indi MP expressed gratitude to bystanders who came to her rescue outside her Wangaratta electorate office.
Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Helen Haines’s first words after alleged attack were about safety of staff and gratitude to bystanders, MP reveals

articles.author: Amy Hawkins in Beijing
articles.description:
The fifth plenum comes against a backdrop of years of purges that have had some analysts wondering if the issue is corruption or a lack of loyalty
When Xi Jinping came to power in 2012, he pledged to stamp out corruption all through the ranks of the Communist party. More than a decade later, the pace of investigations has not slowed. Last year, China’s disciplinary authorities opened investigations into more than 1 million people, including more than 100 officials at or above ministerial or provincial level.
As Chinese Communist party (CCP) officials prepare for an important meeting this week discipline – and party loyalty – is high on the agenda. For those who try to read the tea leaves of elite Chinese politics, concern about the apparent lack of discipline is dominating CCP discussions.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Xi Jinping’s corruption crackdown in the spotlight as China prepares for meeting of top leaders

articles.author: Tom Phillips in São Paulo and Tiago Rogero in Brasília
articles.description:
Leftist incumbent Lula says unprecedented comeback was a ‘defeat for denialism’ as Bolsonaro refuses to accept election result

Lula wins election in stunning comeback – live updates

Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, the Brazilian president, has staged a dramatic election fightback, defeating his far-right opponent, Flávio Bolsonaro, to claim a historic fourth term in power.
With 100% of votes counted the 80-year-old leftist received 51.79% of the vote to his 45-year-old rival’s 48.21%.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Lula wins fourth term as Brazil president after historic upset over far-right Flávio Bolsonaro

articles.author: Seán Clarke and Tom Phillips
articles.description:
After a shock defeat in the first round, the incumbent Brazilian president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, has turned the election around to win the runoff.
Live blog: latest analysis and reaction
Brazil’s president is elected purely by the popular vote. A winning candidate needs one more vote than 50% of votes cast; there is no role for the parliament and no electoral college.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Brazil election 2026: Full second round results as Lula wins comeback against Flávio Bolsonaro

articles.author: Ashifa Kassam, and Ana Milosavljević in Belgrade
articles.description:
Vučić’s 12-year reign looks to have been ended by record turnout of voters in election provoked by student-led protests
The long-serving leader of Serbia, Aleksandar Vučić, has conceded defeat, ushering in a seismic political shift after a historic election that saw ​the increasingly authoritarian leader pitted against a student-led movement that had spent two years protesting against his government.
Vučić pointed to preliminary results that suggested voters had overwhelmingly backed the students, potentially giving them a majority in the country’s 250-seat parliament.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Serbian leader Aleksandar Vučić ousted by student movement in seismic election

articles.author: Jakub Krupa
articles.description:
Student List movement projected to have 141 seats in the new parliament, well clear of the 126 required for majority

Serbian leader Aleksandar Vučić concedes defeat in fiercely contested parliamentary election

The latest turnout projection by Ipsos/Cesid suggests a turnout of 60.8% by 5pm local time (4pm UK), with three hours still to go until the polling stations close.
That’s more than 13 percentage points higher than in 2023, and would be the highest turnout since mid-2000s.
“What hasn’t motivated me? There isn’t a single reason I could give that would keep me from showing up at my polling station at 6:20 in the morning.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Door to EU is open’ new Serbian government told after Vučić concedes election – Europe live as it happened

articles.author: Victoria Bekiempis
articles.description:
Trump again congratulated Ohio senator’s rear end before his cheeky comment about rapper being ‘hard to miss’
Donald Trump reiterated his apparent love for buxom bums during a rally in Michigan on Sunday where he encouraged the crowd to compliment rapper Nicki Minaj’s behind.
Trump’s cheeky comments about Minaj’s derriere came as he explained his recent observation on the Republican Ohio senator Jon Husted’s rear end. Earlier in October, Trump said of the former college football player: “I don’t do this with men very often. I started examining his body, because I didn’t know he was a great athlete. And I looked and I watched up and down. I looked at his ass and I looked at the whole – and then I looked at his hands. Look at his hands. He’s got these, like, claws.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump rallies for Mike Rogers – and Nicki Minaj’s derriere – in Michigan

articles.author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
articles.description:
Downing Street will allocate a further £432m in this week’s budget, bringing total funding for finding a ‘lasting solution’ to nearly £900m
Andy Burnham is to double spending on ending rough sleeping to almost £900m by the end of the current parliament, as he steps up efforts to get people off the streets by Christmas.
The prime minister has pledged to offer every rough sleeper in England a safe route off the streets or wider support as a central part of his premiership.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Burnham to double spending on homelessness amid drive to end rough sleeping by Christmas

articles.author: Hannah Al-Othman and Charlie Moloney
articles.description:
Man aged 60 and another in his 20s killed by falling trees in Scotland and London as Met Office reports gusts of up to 84mph
Two people have been killed and more than 160,000 properties have been left without power as Storm Boelo continues to batter the UK.
Two men, one aged 60 and the other in his 20s, were killed by falling trees on Sunday, police said. The 60-year-old died in south-west Scotland while the man in his 20s was killed in London.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Two dead and 160,000 properties without power as Storm Boelo batters UK

articles.author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
articles.description:
Chancellor is in favour of North Sea project, but energy secretary has said she is leaning towards rejecting it
A cabinet split has emerged over whether to approve drilling at the Rosebank oilfield, with the chancellor, John Healey, in favour of the controversial North Sea project.
The energy secretary, Miatta Fahnbulleh, is ultimately in charge of the decision, and the Guardian reported last week that she was leaning towards rejecting it after granting permission for the smaller Jackdaw gasfield.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Cabinet split emerges over controversial Rosebank oilfield decision

articles.author: Coral Murphy Marcos and agencies
articles.description:
Peltola and her family sustained minor injuries after a driver struck the car transporting group to campaign stop
Mary Peltola, a Democrat who is running for Alaska’s lone US Senate seat, and her family suffered minor injuries in a car crash while driving to a campaign stop on Saturday, her campaign said.
The family was on its way to the Alaska Federation of Natives annual banquet when another vehicle crashed into the one transporting Peltola and her family, her campaign said in a statement on Sunday. Peltola required medical attention after the collision.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Alaska Senate candidate Mary Peltola delays campaign stops after car crash

articles.author: Angelique Chrisafis in Paris
articles.description:
Making innocent protesters liable for damage would be bad for rule of law and play into far-right hands, say opponents
Emmanuel Macron has been accused by trade unions of trying to curb the fundamental French right to protest as the government fast-tracks a bill to make protesters pay for damage caused by vandalism at street demonstrations even if they did not directly cause it themselves.
The French president, who leaves office next spring, has faced more than a month of protests in which high-school students have blockaded schools demanding a response to teacher absences, repairs to decrepit buildings and changes to the university applications platform.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Macron accused of putting France’s right to protest at risk with ‘vandal’s law’

articles.author: Rowena Mason and Jasper Jolly
articles.description:
PM’s plea supported by Angela Rayner, Ed Miliband and business leaders, while some ‘red wall’ MPs voice concern
Andy Burnham’s call for the UK to consider a return to free movement with Europe has been backed by senior cabinet ministers but risked a rift with “red wall” Labour MPs, who say it could jeopardise Brexit-voting seats.
The prime minister made his plea for an “honest discussion” about freedom of movement in an interview with the Sunday Times, making clear that staying out of it would no longer be a red line in talks with the EU.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Cabinet ministers back Burnham’s call for debate on return to free movement with EU

articles.author: Tom Phillips in Rio de Janeiro
articles.description:
Nobel peace prize winner’s return after almost a year in exile is unlikely to please interim president Delcy Rodríguez
The Venezuelan opposition leader, María Corina Machado, has announced she has returned to Venezuela almost a year after she left the country to receive the Nobel peace prize.
“I’m here. With you,” she wrote on X on Sunday lunchtime.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Exiled opposition leader María Corina Machado returns to Venezuela

articles.author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
articles.description:
Chancellor was said to be worried about market-sensitive leaks, yet significant policies have been heavily trailed in the media
The public has been told repeatedly that John Healey is so concerned about budget leaks that he has set up defence-style “compartmentalisation” to prevent the Treasury’s financial secrets escaping.
The macho military analogies began in mid-August when Healey was said by the Telegraph to be “on a war footing” to stop the drip of information that he believed had beleaguered Rachel Reeves.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Has Healey’s military-style budget secrecy really played out so differently to past budgets?

articles.author: Jessica Glenza
articles.description:
Man accused of shooting teen who was driving to a party is also linked to shooting of a vehicle days earlier, police say
A man accused in the shooting death of a Missouri teen has been charged in a second shooting incident – both of which involve firing into cars on the highway.
Alyssa Wilson, 17, was shot and killed as she drove down Interstate 170 in Overland, Missouri, on 14 October. The teen was on her way to a Halloween party at St Louis Zoo, called Boo at the Zoo, when a suspect fired a single shot into the back of Wilson’s Buick Encore.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Suspect in shooting death of Missouri teen on highway charged in second road incident

articles.author: Coral Murphy Marcos and agencies
articles.description:
More inclement weather forecast in rain-soaked Four Corners region after evacuations and rescues last week
Another round of heavy showers and thunderstorms were expected to hit the south-west US on Sunday after the region endured days of rain that forced evacuations, water rescues and multi-million-dollar damage.
The National Weather Service issued a flood watch for much of the Four Corners – the meeting point of Arizona, Colorado, New Mexico and Utah – even as local officials forecast further receding of swollen rivers that surged since rains picked up on Wednesday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US south-west braces for more storms after enduring days of rain and flooding

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
Lana Nusseibeh has Palestine’s endorsement but faces criticism over UAE’s record on human rights and Sudan
An Emirati diplomat who as UAE ambassador to the UN helped secure the delivery of humanitarian aid to Gaza has entered the race as a late contender to succeed António Guterres as the world body’s secretary general.
Lana Nusseibeh, who is of Palestinian heritage, is widely noted for her advocacy of the Palestinian cause and the two-state solution and has won the endorsement of the state of Palestine.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Emirati diplomat who helped deliver aid to Gaza enters UN secretary general race

articles.author: Catherine Shoard
articles.description:
Exclusive: Joshua Loudermilk says suspicions first raised during filming by gun shaped like wearable plastic bottom: ‘You’re gonna put a butt on top of a butt? You can’t run in that’
• This article contains spoilers for Ali G: Who Iz I?
Joshua Loudermilk, one of two men apparently discredited by the new Ali G movie Ali G: Who Iz I?, has said that he was in on the joke, but that the film-makers didn’t realise this.
Loudermilk, a 54-year-old aspiring actor from North Carolina, has told the Guardian he recognised star Sacha Baron Cohen early in the shoot but continued pretending to be a hard-right Maga sympathiser prepared to defend the US border at all costs.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘He’s not going to punk me. I’ll trick him’: Ali G: Who Iz I? stooge says he was in on joke but didn’t tell Sacha Baron Cohen

articles.author: Ashifa Kassam and agencies
articles.description:
More than 30 people arrested as officers clear at least 100 tents in central Lisbon and about 50 in Porto 
Police in Portugal have dismantled housing protest camps in Lisbon and Porto, baton-charging campaigners in the early hours of Sunday and arresting more than 30 people.
The raids were the latest incident in days of clashes between police and campaigners who – inspired by similar camps in Spain – had sought to pitch tents in central squares to protest against the country’s deepening housing crisis.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Portuguese police with dogs and batons dismantle housing protest camps

articles.author: Tiago Rogero in Rio de Janeiro
articles.description:
Incumbent president lost in first round to senator and son of convicted ex-president 
Brazilians are going to the polls on Sunday in a highly unpredictable runoff in which the leftist president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, is attempting an unprecedented comeback against the far-right senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who won the first-round vote.
Bolsonaro’s surprise victory despite not leading most polls made him the favourite three weeks ago, but since then Lula’s campaign has gained ground, and the two go into the contest virtually tied.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Brazilians vote in presidential election runoff pitting leftist Lula against far-right Bolsonaro

articles.author: Jasper Jolly and agencies
articles.description:
VW investment, creating 4,500 jobs in Georgia, comes amid Trump’s damaging tariffs, intense Chinese competition and costly shift towards EVs
Audi has said it will spend $4bn (£3bn) to build its first factory in the US, as its parent company, Volkswagen, struggles with the impact of steep tariffs imposed by Donald Trump.
The German brand’s chief executive, Gernot Döllner, joined Trump on stage at a campaign rally on Saturday night to announce the factory in Macon, Georgia, in an unusual move by a big European brand just days before the US midterm elections.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Volkswagen to build $4bn Audi SUV factory in US despite job cuts at home

articles.author: Oliver Holmes and Caroline Davies
articles.description:
Exclusive: Forensic analysis of found images continues as Meghan’s father denies possessing child sexual abuse images
All signs point to Thomas Markle Sr being a “possible sex offender of the grossest kind” although a full forensic investigation will give a “definitive picture”, the Philippine interior minister has told the Guardian.
Authorities in the south-east Asian country are analysing digital images allegedly belonging to the estranged father of the Duchess of Sussex that were said to have been found at his former home in Cebu. Meghan’s half-brother, Thomas Markle Jr, reported to authorities last week that he had apparently discovered a stash of child sexual abuse images.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Signs suggest Thomas Markle Sr may be ‘sex offender of the grossest kind’, says Philippine minister

articles.author: Julian Borger in Jerusalem
articles.description:
PM Benjamin Netanyahu vows ‘to destroy this place’ in retaliation for militant attack on army checkpoint
Israeli troops have levelled a neighbourhood in Hebron, driving out hundreds of families in collective punishment for a militant attack on an army checkpoint outside the West Bank city, local Palestinian authorities said.
The Hebron municipality estimated that 35 hectares (86 acres) had been destroyed or marked for destruction and about 1,500 people had been evicted from their homes by Saturday afternoon in the district of Ein Deir Baha. The whole city of 250,000 people was sealed off by checkpoints on every point of entry.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Israeli soldiers raze neighbourhood in Hebron, driving families from homes

articles.author: Josh Halliday
articles.description:
The story of the emirates’ presence in Manchester winds from the Arab Spring to some of the most deprived places in England – with complicated results 

Emirati-linked firms’ ownership of Manchester land ‘up 39%’ in 10 years


When Hosni Mubarak, Egypt’s long-ruling dictator, was toppled from power in the Arab spring protests of 2011, his downfall sent shock waves across the Middle East. It also helped change the face of modern Manchester.
Mubarak’s successor, the Muslim Brotherhood leader Mohamed Morsi, was a sworn enemy of the United Arab Emirates, whose rulers feared the advance of Morsi’s Islamism.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘That’s the way the city works’: how the UAE changed the face of Andy Burnham’s Manchester

articles.author: Seham Tantesh in Gaza and Lorenzo Tondo
articles.description:
Humanitarian catastrophe largely ignored as rivals Gadi Eisenkot and Benjamin Netanyahu vow to end Hamas rule
As Israel prepares to go to the polls, Palestinians in Gaza are bracing for an outcome that could shape their future, knowing their fate rests with the country that has reduced much of the territory to rubble and killed nearly 75,000 people.
Gaza, where nearly a million displaced Palestinians face dire sanitary conditions, water shortages and the constant threat of Israeli strikes, has been largely absent from the election campaign.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Gaza’s suffering has become campaign fodder’: Palestinians fear the worst from Israel election

articles.author: Oliver Holmes in Bangkok
articles.description:
Kim Aris tells the Guardian chance to speak with detained Nobel laureate was ‘public relations’ move from military leaders
Myanmar’s former democratic leader Aung San Suu Kyi appears to be in good physical and mental health but is living in near-complete isolation, her son has said after the first call with his 81-year-old mother in more than five years.
“She still sounds certainly all there mentally, and physically she sounds strong,” Kim Aris said. “I don’t think she has anybody outside of the military or the police around her, so essentially she’s been held in solitary confinement from what I gather.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Myanmar’s Aung San Suu Kyi ‘sounds strong’ but is isolated, son says

articles.author: Reuters in Al-Mushairfeh
articles.description:
Footage broadcast on state TV shows three attackers approaching Greek Orthodox church and firing shots
Nine people have been killed after gunmen opened fire at a funeral at a church in Jordan in a rare attack ⁠on the country’s Christian minority.
Authorities described the attack on Friday as a terrorist act by extremists.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Nine killed and 40 injured after gunmen open fire at church funeral in Jordan

articles.author: Raphael Rashid in Seoul
articles.description:
North Korean leader travels over New Yalu River Bridge to meet senior Communist party member
Kim Jong-un has visited China, inaugurating a bridge that connects the two countries and saying he hopes to expand cooperation with his neighbour.
The North Korean leader arrived in the Chinese border city of Dandong on Saturday after crossing the New Yalu River Bridge, according to South Korea’s unification ministry, which handles affairs related to North Korea, and China’s official Xinhua news agency.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Kim Jong-un crosses newly opened bridge into China

articles.author: Reuters
articles.description:
Super typhoon weakening but large parts of Taiwan, including Taipei, still mostly closed and flights cancelled
Typhoon Champi swept past Taiwan on Saturday killing one person, injuring more than 500, and uprooting trees and severing power as it weakened and ⁠headed north toward ⁠the ​Chinese coast.
Earlier classified as a super typhoon and one of the strongest storms in the ⁠Pacific this year, Champi was still packing gusts of about 126km per hour (78 miles per hour) near its ⁠centre, according to Taiwan’s Central Weather Administration (CWA).
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Typhoon Champi kills one and injures more than 500 in Taiwan as it heads to China

articles.author: Caroline Davies
articles.description:
Meghan reveals she was made aware of ‘disturbing allegations’ against him in 2018 by Met police
The Duchess of Sussex has said she is “deeply distressed” over accusations involving child sexual abuse images against her estranged father, Thomas Markle Sr, and revealed she was made aware of “disturbing allegations” against him in 2018 by the Metropolitan police.
Meghan issued a statement after the Sun newspaper published claims that her half-brother Thomas Markle Jr alleged he had found a stash of images belonging to their father at his former home in the Philippines.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Duchess of Sussex ‘deeply distressed’ over child sexual abuse image claims against father

articles.author: Carlos Mureithi in Nairobi and agencies
articles.description:
Switzerland says patient is wife of Swiss diplomat and believed to have contracted virus while travelling in Uganda
Health officials across Africa are racing to determine how Nigeria’s first Ebola patient ⁠in more than a decade ⁠became infected, amid fears ​the outbreak could spread further after reaching a fourth African country.
The Swiss foreign ministry said on Friday the patient in Nigeria, the Ugandan-born wife of a Swiss diplomat based in Abuja, had not travelled to the Democratic Republic of ⁠Congo, where the outbreak was first detected in mid-May before spreading to Uganda, Kenya and now Nigeria. The woman was believed to have contracted Ebola while travelling with her husband in Uganda, the ministry added.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Mystery over source of Ebola infection in Nigeria fuels concern about spread of virus

articles.author: Amrit Dhillon in Delhi
articles.description:
Case filed in 2022 by patient unable to afford medicine leads to cap on drug prices for millions who face ruin if diagnosed
The Indian government has moved to reduce the price of cancer drugs after a retired bank clerk took her case to the supreme court.
From next month, 137 cancer drugs in India will be cheaper as the government tries to tackle the tragedy of poorer patients either forgoing treatment, selling land or falling into debt to meet the high cost of some medicines, which are making large profits for hospitals and pharmacists.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: India slashes cost of cancer drugs after court rules mark-ups are ‘extortion’

articles.author: Giles Richards in Austin
articles.description:
41-year-old set on ‘dream to be able to race in Africa’

Rwanda to host despite criticism of human rights record

Lewis Hamilton has said he hopes to remain racing in Formula One until he can take part in the African Grand Prix which is set to take place in Rwanda in the 2030s. The seven-time world champion believes it is right that F1 is to hold a race there despite criticism of the country’s human rights record.
Last week F1 confirmed Rwanda was to host the African Grand Prix having concluded a 10-year agreement for the meeting on a purpose-built circuit, with the first race set for the early 2030s. It is lined up to be held on a circuit in Bugesera, 25 miles south of the capital, Kigali, which has yet to be constructed and marks a return to the African continent for the first time since it last held a race at Kyalami, South Africa in 1993.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Lewis Hamilton aims to extend career till early 2030s so he can race in African Grand Prix

articles.author: Agence France-Presse in Yangon
articles.description:
Kim Aris says ‘hearing her voice again means more than words can express’ amid loosening of detention restrictions
The son of Myanmar’s Aung San Suu Kyi has been allowed to speak to the detained former democratic leader for the first time in more than five years.
“Today, I was finally able to speak with my mother, Daw Aung San Suu Kyi, after more than five years. Hearing her voice again means more than words can express,” Kim Aris said in a post on Facebook on Thursday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Aung San Suu Kyi’s son speaks to detained former Myanmar leader for first time in five years

articles.author: Melody Schreiber
articles.description:
Hepatitis B study in Guinea-Bissau that was to be funded by CDC and that drew global backlash ‘will not move forward’
The US-backed hepatitis B vaccine trial in African newborns that drew global backlash was halted, the lead researcher said on Wednesday.
It was “now clear” that the study “will not move forward in Guinea-Bissau”, Frederik Schaltz-Buchholzer, a Danish researcher, wrote on LinkedIn, adding, “we were not given the necessary governmental approval.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Controversial US-backed vaccine trial in African newborns halted

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka spent a week in jail after defying restrictions on protests in Delhi amid government crackdown
An Indian court has ordered the release of two leaders of India’s Cockroach movement who were jailed last week amid a mounting state crackdown on youth-led protests.
The two leaders of the Cockroach Janta party (CJP) movement, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, had spent a week in Delhi’s Tihar jail after being arrested by Delhi police last week.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Indian court orders release of two leaders of Cockroach movement

articles.author: Richard Luscombe in Miami
articles.description:
Flights to third countries where the detainees have no ties are scheduled as early as Wednesday, relatives detail

Send us your questions about immigration and the midterms

Relatives of gravely ill detainees at two Florida immigration jails say authorities are about to deport their loved ones to unknown countries in Africa despite worsening medical conditions.
Flights are scheduled as early as Wednesday, according to the families and the immigration advocacy group the Workers Circle, which has been monitoring conditions and speaking with detainees inside two Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) facilities in south Florida.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Severely ill ICE detainees face imminent deportation to unknown African states, advocates say

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Case in Africa’s most populous country was detected in a woman who had travelled from Uganda
Nigeria has confirmed an Ebola case in its capital, Abuja, after a woman who arrived from Uganda tested positive for the virus, the health ministry said.
The woman began showing symptoms on 7 October and was admitted to a hospital in Abuja four days later, where she was later diagnosed with Ebola. It is unclear when she arrived in Nigeria, Africa’s most populous country.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Nigeria confirms Ebola case as outbreak spreads into western Africa

articles.author: Julia Kollewe
articles.description:
Low-cost broadband provider Jio Platforms aims for £81bn valuation when it floats on the stock market on Wednesday
India’s second-richest man, Mukesh Ambani, is launching what could be the country’s biggest-ever initial public offering (IPO), despite a stock market downturn.
Mumbai-based Jio Platforms, a telecoms company backed by Meta Platforms and Google, is hoping to raise up to 302bn rupees (£2.4bn) and is targeting a 10.3tn rupees valuation when it floats on the stock market from Wednesday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Billionaire Mukesh Ambani launches India’s biggest-ever IPO

articles.author: Victoria Bekiempis
articles.description:
Trump again congratulated Ohio senator’s rear end before his cheeky comment about rapper being ‘hard to miss’
Donald Trump reiterated his apparent love for buxom bums during a rally in Michigan on Sunday where he encouraged the crowd to compliment rapper Nicki Minaj’s behind.
Trump’s cheeky comments about Minaj’s derriere came as he explained his recent observation on the Republican Ohio senator Jon Husted’s rear end. Earlier in October, Trump said of the former college football player: “I don’t do this with men very often. I started examining his body, because I didn’t know he was a great athlete. And I looked and I watched up and down. I looked at his ass and I looked at the whole – and then I looked at his hands. Look at his hands. He’s got these, like, claws.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump rallies for Mike Rogers – and Nicki Minaj’s derriere – in Michigan

articles.author: Coral Murphy Marcos and agencies
articles.description:
Peltola and her family sustained minor injuries after a driver struck the car transporting group to campaign stop
Mary Peltola, a Democrat who is running for Alaska’s lone US Senate seat, and her family suffered minor injuries in a car crash while driving to a campaign stop on Saturday, her campaign said.
The family was on its way to the Alaska Federation of Natives annual banquet when another vehicle crashed into the one transporting Peltola and her family, her campaign said in a statement on Sunday. Peltola required medical attention after the collision.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Alaska Senate candidate Mary Peltola delays campaign stops after car crash

articles.author: Victoria Bekiempis
articles.description:
US attorney general calls CNN ‘crazy’ for suggesting Trump’s attempt to overturn election could lead to January 6 repeat

Sign up for The Stakes 2026: your weekly guide to the US midterms

Todd Blanche, Donald Trump’s attorney general, lashed out during an interview on Sunday while defending the justice department’s pre-emptive lawsuit to block certification of Alaska’s US Senate results if the GOP incumbent loses, calling a TV host’s question “crazy”.
The testy repartee unfolded on CNN’s State of the Union over the DoJ’s unprecedented legal action, which alleges that there could be “voter confusion” due to two candidates named Dan Sullivan on Alaska’s ballot. Trump told reporters, “I’m the one that said do it” when asked about the suit.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Blanche defends DoJ’s pre-emptive suit to block Alaska Senate results certification

articles.author: Rachel Leingang in Arthur, Nebraska
articles.description:
Democratic and independent candidates stump the US midwest and prairie states, hoping to win over Republican strongholds
In this final stretch of the US midterm elections, Democrats and independents could win back communities and towns across America’s rural heartlands through a combination of resurgent “prairie populism”, local despair over the impact of Donald Trump’s agenda and an old-fashioned tenet of shoe-leather politics: showing up everywhere.
When Dan Osborn rolled into one of the most rural counties in Nebraska earlier this month, he started walking into businesses in the tiny main drag of Arthur, ready to meet whomever he could in the town of about 100.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Prairie Populists’ fight to win back rural voters long ceded to Republicans

articles.author: Andrew Gumbel in Lone Pine, California
articles.description:
How a rebuilt, historic California baseball diamond embodies ‘the contradictions in America’s legacy’
When Dan Kwong first dreamed of staging baseball games at the Japanese American concentration camp where his family was held captive during the second world war, he thought of it as an exercise in living history, an eye-catching way to convey the trauma of 120,000 men, women and children who were locked up in the wake of the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor.
Baseball was a passion for Kwong, a 71-year-old performance artist from Los Angeles. He knew that the wartime internees had played the game not just as a distraction from their predicament, but as a quiet expression of their loyalty to the United States. He wanted to stage an event that would cast the game as an act of resistance, and teach new generations about the damage governments do when they strip a whole segment of the population of their constitutional rights.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: A child of Japanese incarceration’s call to arms: ‘The lessons of Manzanar have never been more urgent’

articles.description:
Barack Obama headlined a rally for Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic nominee for the US Senate, in Detroit on the first day of early voting in Michigan. The former US president told thousands of supporters at Cass technical high school that the 3 November election was an 'inflection point' for American politics

Obama rallies rapturous Michigan crowd for El-Sayed: ‘He’ll finish the job we started’

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Obama throws support behind El-Sayed as early voting begins in Michigan – video

articles.author: David Smith in Washington
articles.description:
James Blair’s data-driven approach delivered victory in 2024 but president’s unpopularity and idiosyncratic style do not bode well this time
They are both young, bald and fathers of four. They are also the brains behind Donald Trump. But while Stephen Miller is infamous as the US president’s ideological enforcer, James Blair could, in the words of Time magazine, “be the most important person in Donald Trump’s Washington you’ve never heard of”.
That imbalance is deceptive, however. Blair has sufficiently impressed Trump to earn the nickname “Brilliant James”. And a well-positioned source told the Guardian: “I would say that James is probably twice, five times, 10 times more effective than Stephen Miller.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Brilliant James’ helped return Trump to the White House. Can he conquer the midterms?

articles.author: Julian Borger Senior international correspondent
articles.description:
Brazil, Israel, Serbia and the US are holding elections within the space of 10 days. Will the authoritarian right cement its global gains, or can pro-democracy forces make a comeback?
Four elections on four continents within 10 days could profoundly reshape global politics, propelling the world further along its current authoritarian trajectory or marking a limited comeback for democratic norms.
In all four contests, basic democratic norms are at stake at a time when autocracy is advancing worldwide at an alarming rate. According to the Sweden-based V-Dem Institute, which uses multivariable assessment tools, the democratic freedoms enjoyed by the average global citizen are down to levels last seen in 1978 – long before the fall of the Berlin Wall and the collapse of communism in Europe.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ten days that could shake the world: democratic norms at stake in four pivotal elections

articles.author: Ariana Baio in New Jersey
articles.description:
Even with a multimillion-dollar war chest, the US representative faces a stiff fight for his seat from Democrat Rebecca Bennett
The stars above New Jersey seemed aligned for Tom Kean Jr.
The Republican congressman had a war chest of more than $2.4m in February, an endorsement from Donald Trump and a district whose lines were redrawn in 2022 to benefit his party. He was an established political figure with widespread name recognition, thanks to his father’s stint as a well-regarded governor of New Jersey.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Tom Kean had everything going for him. Then the Republican New Jersey congressman disappeared

articles.author: Robert Tait
articles.description:
Vice-president’s visibility has risen as Trump’s popularity wanes, but path to inherit Maga throne is more complicated than it may seem
A day after JD Vance suggested Donald Trump would endorse him if he runs for president, the vice-president shifted awkwardly in the Oval Office as his boss was asked about the remark.
“He’s a very talented person, and he’s a very good person,” Trump said of the man standing behind him, with a forced smile this week. “But we’ve literally – I don’t think we’ve ever talked about,” the president claimed, leaving the assertion unconfirmed.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Vance front and center in Republican midterms push – is this a dry run for a White House bid?

articles.author: Steve Bloomfield
articles.description:
We’ve heard much about the end of the west. At the proposed summit between Trump, Putin and Xi, those fears could crystallise
In the final two years of a US presidency, when Congress has been lost, approval ratings have sunk like a stone and their party has started to think about who’s coming next, the person occupying the Oval Office can feel their power draining away. Domestic legislation, particularly in an era where bipartisan cooperation is almost nonexistent, grinds to a halt. But as the days tick by until the end, and as presidents begin to think about their legacy, there is one part of the job where they still have power: the rest of the world.
In the final weeks of his presidency in 1992 George HW Bush sent 28,000 American troops to Somalia to help end a famine. For Bill Clinton, it was a quixotic attempt to bring peace to the Middle East by ending the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. Barack Obama restored diplomatic ties with Cuba, making a historic visit to Havana, as well as a final, successful push on the Iran nuclear deal.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: As Trump’s time runs out, this could be his most dangerous legacy: a world divided into three | Steve Bloomfield

articles.description:
Donald Trump told rally-goers on Thursday evening that he had 'the right to run again' for president, invoking a claim he has repeatedly made that he may seek a third term despite it being unconstitutional
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump floats unconstitutional third term at campaign rally in Iowa – video

articles.author: Moira Donegan
articles.description:
Republicans are resorting to childish taunts to defend an uncommonly dishonorable state attorney general
It’s a bit like Lucy with the football. Every few years, Democrats convince themselves that a Texas Senate seat might finally switch from red to blue. On paper, it makes sense. Texas is a large and urbanizing state with an increasingly educated – and increasingly non-white – population.
Other one-time Republican strongholds that have undergone similar demographic shifts have turned purple or even blueish – think Georgia, for example. The border counties along the Rio Grande valley, with their deep poverty and big Latino populations, were long thought to be fertile ground to nurture a kind of anti-Trump populism that could be converted into pro-Democratic sentiment. The state Democratic party is anemic there, but a few talented candidates have emerged.
Moira Donegan is a Guardian US columnist
 Continue reading...
articles.title: A Democratic win in Texas is a long shot – but Ken Paxton’s weakness is obvious | Moira Donegan

articles.author: Sidney Blumenthal
articles.description:
The US president is portraying Zelenskyy as the villain as he strives for Russia’s approval
If Donald Trump could, he would fly to Munich to sign away Ukraine to Vladimir Putin, and return to wave the document as “peace in our time”, hoping to claim at least the second Fifa peace prize.
Whatever the complicated motives of Neville Chamberlain, his well-grounded fear after the carnage of a world war of another apocalypse and his wishful thinking that Hitler would be satiated after carving up Czechoslovakia, Chamberlain had not sent his son-in-law and former golf partner and real estate partner in advance to cut back-end deals with the Nazis to profit for his family and cronies.
Sidney Blumenthal, former senior adviser to Bill Clinton and Hillary Clinton, has published three books of a projected five-volume political life of Abraham Lincoln: A Self-Made Man, Wrestling With His Angel and All the Powers of Earth. He is a Guardian US columnist and co-host of the Court of History podcast
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The Trump-Putin love story’s next chapter: selling out Ukraine | Sidney Blumenthal

articles.author: Shrai Popat, Hazel Tang, John Farrell, Karif Wat
articles.description:
To reclaim control of the Senate, Democrats need to retain all the Senate seats they have and flip four more in the 2026 midterm elections.  Shrai Popat, the Guardian's US politics reporter, explains which are the key races to watch in November.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: These key races in the 2026 midterms will decide who controls the US Senate – video explainer

articles.author: Robert Reich
articles.description:
The president shows a unique disregard for the opinions, norms and ideals of the nation – and, for that matter, humanity
The Democrats’ focus on affordability seems to be a winning strategy (we’ll know for sure in a little over two weeks). But we mustn’t lose sight of the moral squalor at the core of the Trump regime and the necessity of ending it.
It’s that moral squalor – the utter disregard for the opinions, norms and ideals of the nation and, for that matter, of humanity – that uniquely marks Trump and the reprobates he has attracted to Washington. It has also poisoned much of the Republican party, including the billionaires and tech bros who finance it.
Robert Reich, a former US secretary of labor, is a professor of public policy emeritus at the University of California, Berkeley. He is a Guardian US columnist and his newsletter is at robertreich.substack.com. His new book, Coming Up Short: A Memoir of My America, is out now in the US and in the UK
 Continue reading...
articles.title: America must reverse Trump’s moral squalor | Robert Reich

articles.author: Oliver Laughland, Tom Silverstone, Katie Lamborn, Jem Talbot, Ivan Kuraev
articles.description:
A battle for Alabama’s second congressional district is being fought against a backdrop of partisan gerrymandering and America’s ongoing civil rights struggle. Oliver Laughland and Tom Silverstone track down the Maga Republican Rhett Marques who is looking to unseat Democratic incumbent Shomari Figures but won’t answer questions about redistricting. Meanwhile, lower-income residents in rural parts of the district are still fighting for basic sanitation rights after Donald Trump ended federal assistance, which the administration described as 'illegal DEI'.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How Alabama's Republicans are disenfranchising Black voters – video

articles.author: Presented by Helen Pidd with Josh Halliday; produced by Tom Glasser, Scarlet Pestell, Claudia Efemini and Ross Burns; executive producer Sami Kent
articles.description:
After the prime minister recently intervened to defend Manchester City’s beleaguered ownership, many began to ask: just how deep are the ties between Andy Burnham and the UAE? With North of England editor Josh Halliday. Send your comments and questions to tif.questions@theguardian.com
Why did Andy Burnham recently intervene to defend Manchester City’s beleaguered Abu Dhabi owners, days after they were found guilty of one of the biggest cheating scandals in British sporting history?
Today in Focus presenter and city resident Helen Pidd walks through modern Manchester – where Burnham was mayor for nearly a decade – and charts its transformation wrought by Emirati money.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How Abu Dhabi bought Andy Burnham’s Manchester - podcast

articles.author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
articles.description:
Downing Street will allocate a further £432m in this week’s budget, bringing total funding for finding a ‘lasting solution’ to nearly £900m
Andy Burnham is to double spending on ending rough sleeping to almost £900m by the end of the current parliament, as he steps up efforts to get people off the streets by Christmas.
The prime minister has pledged to offer every rough sleeper in England a safe route off the streets or wider support as a central part of his premiership.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Burnham to double spending on homelessness amid drive to end rough sleeping by Christmas

articles.author: Hannah Al-Othman and Charlie Moloney
articles.description:
Man aged 60 and another in his 20s killed by falling trees in Scotland and London as Met Office reports gusts of up to 84mph
Two people have been killed and more than 160,000 properties have been left without power as Storm Boelo continues to batter the UK.
Two men, one aged 60 and the other in his 20s, were killed by falling trees on Sunday, police said. The 60-year-old died in south-west Scotland while the man in his 20s was killed in London.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Two dead and 160,000 properties without power as Storm Boelo batters UK

articles.author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
articles.description:
Chancellor is in favour of North Sea project, but energy secretary has said she is leaning towards rejecting it
A cabinet split has emerged over whether to approve drilling at the Rosebank oilfield, with the chancellor, John Healey, in favour of the controversial North Sea project.
The energy secretary, Miatta Fahnbulleh, is ultimately in charge of the decision, and the Guardian reported last week that she was leaning towards rejecting it after granting permission for the smaller Jackdaw gasfield.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Cabinet split emerges over controversial Rosebank oilfield decision

articles.author: Rowena Mason and Jasper Jolly
articles.description:
PM’s plea supported by Angela Rayner, Ed Miliband and business leaders, while some ‘red wall’ MPs voice concern
Andy Burnham’s call for the UK to consider a return to free movement with Europe has been backed by senior cabinet ministers but risked a rift with “red wall” Labour MPs, who say it could jeopardise Brexit-voting seats.
The prime minister made his plea for an “honest discussion” about freedom of movement in an interview with the Sunday Times, making clear that staying out of it would no longer be a red line in talks with the EU.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Cabinet ministers back Burnham’s call for debate on return to free movement with EU

articles.author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
articles.description:
Chancellor was said to be worried about market-sensitive leaks, yet significant policies have been heavily trailed in the media
The public has been told repeatedly that John Healey is so concerned about budget leaks that he has set up defence-style “compartmentalisation” to prevent the Treasury’s financial secrets escaping.
The macho military analogies began in mid-August when Healey was said by the Telegraph to be “on a war footing” to stop the drip of information that he believed had beleaguered Rachel Reeves.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Has Healey’s military-style budget secrecy really played out so differently to past budgets?

articles.author: Charlie Moloney
articles.description:
Police say the incident at an address in Barking is not believed to be suspicious
A four-year-old girl has died after falling from a tower block in east London.
She was injured after “falling from height” at an address in St Paul’s Road, Barking, on Saturday and died in hospital, the Metropolitan police said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Four-year-old girl dies after falling from east London tower block

articles.author: George Francis Lee
articles.description:
Number of videos about British trains doubles in three months as creators find audiences interested in workings of railways
They are not just gathered at the end of your local train station platform any more. Now they are on your social media platforms too.
Trainspotters have played a part in more than doubling the number of videos about British trains on TikTok in the last three months. According to the platform, the rise in rail content is also down to more people seeking information on cheap tickets, facts about the London Underground and tales from train staff.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: All aboard the TrainTok trend: spotters and staff boost rail content online

articles.author: Tobi Thomas Health and inequalities correspondent
articles.description:
Exclusive: People from marginalised groups more likely to be diagnosed via urgent referral or in emergency setting, research finds 
People from minority ethnic backgrounds in England are up to a third less likely to be diagnosed with breast cancer via routine screening, and are more likely to be diagnosed in an emergency setting, analysis has found.
The research, carried out by academics at the University of Surrey and funded by the charity Breast Cancer Now, involved analysis of 86,564 adults diagnosed with the disease between 2009 and 2019, from the Clinical Practice Research Datalink and the Cancer Registration Tumour and Treatment datasets.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ethnic minorities in England less likely to get breast cancer diagnosis from routine screening

articles.author: Ben Quinn and Jessica Elgot
articles.description:
Sources close to Tory leader say Jack Ross, who faces party investigation after undercover report, worked as social media consultant
A former Conservative election candidate who was suspended after he was filmed discussing the cost of hiring contract killers worked as a consultant in Kemi Badenoch’s office as recently as last year.
Jack Ross is facing an investigation by the Tories after he was filmed apparently asking an undercover reporter: “What do you want done?” and apparently offering to “broker” the services of an alleged far-right paramilitary group.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Former Tory candidate suspended over contract killer claims was adviser in Kemi Badenoch’s office

articles.author: Graeme Wearden
articles.description:
Experts say Bank of England  unlikely to increase rates by full percentage point – and could lower them by end of 2027
Financial markets are wrong to predict the Bank of England will raise UK interest rates by a full percentage point or more by next summer, City economists believe.
According to market-implied interest rate expectations, the Bank is likely to raise interest rates at least four times over the next year, lifting the bank rate from 3.75% today to 4.75% by the end of July, and possibly to 5% – meaning five rises – by December 2027.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Interest rates unlikely to reach 4.75% by next summer, say City economists

articles.author: Haroon Siddique Legal affairs correspondent
articles.description:
Irish and Welsh authors Chris Haughton and Nicola Davies show solidarity after Rooney’s support for Palestine Action
The children’s laureates for Ireland and Wales are donating royalties from their works to Sally Rooney in a show of solidarity after she was forced to stop selling books in the UK because of her support for Palestine Action.
Chris Haughton, Ireland’s children’s literature laureate, said he also wanted to demonstrate the “absurdity” of the bestselling author being unable to receive royalties from her own UK sales because of her public support for the direct action group.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Two children’s laureates to give royalties to Sally Rooney after her UK sales halted

articles.author: Natricia Duncan
articles.description:
Police closed case of Andrew Frederick despite autopsy report ruling his death a homicide
A time-critical investigation into the death of a British father whose body was found in a ransacked property on the Caribbean island of Grenada has stalled because of diplomatic delays between the two countries.
Charity workers supporting the family of Andrew Frederick are demanding immediate government intervention to clear the path for a full investigation to begin almost 10 months after his death, which has been ruled a homicide by a pathologist.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Demand for UK government action 10 months after British man’s death in Grenada

articles.author: Mark Brown North of England correspondent
articles.description:
Teesside town has come out worst in children’s commissioner’s report, but residents say such rankings are demoralising and counterproductive
“It’s disappointing, it’s just another kicking,” said a youth worker after the town in which they work was labelled as the hardest place in which to be a child in England.
“It suggests our children are living unhappy lives,” said a teacher, who described her pupils as joyful.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Why would I leave?’: Middlesbrough pushes back against ‘hardest place to grow up’ label

articles.author: Simon Goodley
articles.description:
Andrew Woosnam took millions from his recruitment firms before creditors, including HMRC, were left out of pocket
• Companies revived in ‘phoenix’ deals more likely to fail, study finds

For three decades, the recruitment industry treated Andrew Woosnam well.
Having learned his trade during the 1990s, he graduated to create his own firm at the turn of the millennium – which allowed him to bank millions of pounds in salary, dividends and loans and to buy assets including a grand house in Berkshire once owned by the comedians Dawn French and Lenny Henry.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The boss whose twice-bust business appears to be back despite £3m debts

articles.author: Simon Goodley
articles.description:
Exclusive: research for the Guardian shows ‘pre-pack’ deals with former management also pay far less to creditors

The boss whose twice-bust business appears to be back

Insolvent businesses reacquired by their previous management in “pre-pack” administrations are much more likely to fail again and tend to repay far less to creditors, research for the Guardian suggests.
The study is the latest to raise questions about the practice of “phoenixism” – accounting’s controversial art of liquidating companies to allow directors to return with a new entity, free of debts.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Bust companies revived in ‘phoenix’ deals more likely to fail again, study finds

articles.author: Presented by Aditya Chakrabortty, produced by Frankie Tobi and Luke John Smith; the executive producers are Maz Ebtehaj, Kirsty Major and James Tindale
articles.description:
Are we doomscrolling our way into a democratic crisis? That’s what the playwright James Graham fears may be happening, as he suggests that our algorithms have led us into ‘a massive crisis of the new’ and are preventing us from imagining a different future
Watch the full episode with James Graham here.
INK, based on James Graham’s stage play, will be released in UK cinemas on 8 January 2027.
Dear England: about the country’s football team under manager Gareth Southgate.
Sherwood (mentioned in the conversation): set in the village where James grew up in the shadow of the miners’ strike.
Quiz: documenting a notorious scandal on the British gameshow Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Culture is stagnant, so politics is stuck’ – playwright James Graham | Radical Thinking – podcast

articles.author: Rachel Hall
articles.description:
Reality TV show returns to focus on childbirth, diversity and the sharing of stories in a social media age
When One Born Every Minute first aired in 2010, viewers loved its fly-on-the-wall take on life in a maternity unit, from midwives idly chatting about unusual pregnancy cravings to parents squabbling over whether to call their child Zeus.
Almost two decades later, as the show is rebooted for a generation who spend their lives on social media, much has changed. Parents now share far more about their struggles with miscarriages, infertility and mental health; audiences have to be lured away from watching reels on their phones with more rigorous storytelling.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘I can’t believe I get to see that’: One Born Every Minute is back for a 12th series

articles.author: Sarah Butler
articles.description:
In the third article in a series on high-end British manufacturing, we visit the Ettinger factory in Walsall

‘Our town is making jeans again’: reviving jobs and skills in Wales

From feathers to pet portraits, Rolls-Royce rides high on custom craze


“It is all down to attention to detail and everything we do is based around that.”
Gary Billingham is demonstrating how the 28 pieces which make up an Ettinger wallet are cut from leather using a hydraulic press by the small team at one of Walsall’s last remaining leather goods factories. The edges of the pieces are thinned down so they are ready to be turned, glued and stitched together by hand.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘You can’t bring in robots’: the leather firm handmaking everything from wallets to cigar cases

articles.author: Michael Goodier
articles.description:
Sewage samples and crime statistics paint a picture of established users taking more cocaine, more often

Cocaine-linked crimes on the rise in Britain as consumption surges

Pubs, festivals and workplaces: how cocaine has become an everyday habit

From pub toilets and private parties to football terraces and far-right marches, cocaine has become a familiar presence across modern Britain. Deaths linked to the drug have risen to record levels, while its supply supports a multibillion-pound criminal industry.
But who is using the drug, and how has the picture changed? The figures do not necessarily show millions of new users, but highlight an established market in which some people take more cocaine, more often – and face greater harm as they grow older.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ageing users and record deaths – the data behind Britain’s multibillion-pound cocaine habit

articles.author: Ella Creamer
articles.description:
Novelist says demise of Britain’s ‘incredible’ welfare system and housing struggles have led to deeper divisions
The novelist Zadie Smith has said that inequality has made culture clashes feel “existential”, adding that it has become “natural to look to your left and think ‘who the fuck are you?’”
In an interview with Dua Lipa as part of the Southbank Centre’s London literature festival, Smith argued that the demise of Britain’s “incredible, historic” welfare system has led to greater divisions.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Zadie Smith tells Dua Lipa inequality has made culture clashes feel ‘existential’

articles.author: Josh Halliday
articles.description:
The story of the emirates’ presence in Manchester winds from the Arab Spring to some of the most deprived places in England – with complicated results 

Emirati-linked firms’ ownership of Manchester land ‘up 39%’ in 10 years


When Hosni Mubarak, Egypt’s long-ruling dictator, was toppled from power in the Arab spring protests of 2011, his downfall sent shock waves across the Middle East. It also helped change the face of modern Manchester.
Mubarak’s successor, the Muslim Brotherhood leader Mohamed Morsi, was a sworn enemy of the United Arab Emirates, whose rulers feared the advance of Morsi’s Islamism.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘That’s the way the city works’: how the UAE changed the face of Andy Burnham’s Manchester

articles.author: Patrick Daly
articles.description:
Prime minister is considering different options for new relationship with Brussels ahead of summit in November
Andy Burnham says he wants an “honest discussion” with the British public about the possibility of a return to free movement between the UK and the EU as part of his plans for a new relationship with the bloc.
The prime minister has been open about his desire to revisit the relationship between Britain and Brussels. He has said a new deal could mean the UK goes “all the way” and rejoins the EU.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Andy Burnham says he wants ‘honest discussion’ about freedom of movement with EU

articles.author: Press Association
articles.description:
Fresh deluge of wet weather comes after Storm Austen brought strong winds to many regions on Friday
Amber weather warnings have come into force as the worst of Storm Boelo could be set to hit parts of the UK.
Storm Boelo’s winds will peak from Saturday evening, leaving areas in the warning zone, including Scotland, parts of Northern Ireland and the far north of England, braced for gusts of 60-70mph and even 80mph in exposed coastal spots, the Met Office said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Storm Boelo: Travel disrupted and events cancelled as UK hit by wind and rain

articles.author: Heather Stewart Economics editor
articles.description:
Chancellor will build on Burnham’s promise that local leaders in England will no longer have to ‘come cap in hand to Westminster’
Andy Burnham has promised that local leaders in England will no longer have to come “cap in hand to Westminster” ahead of a fresh drive to devolve spending power in next week’s budget.
In his statement on Wednesday, the chancellor, John Healey, will include plans for a new £1.5bn borrowing facility, to be drawn up in collaboration with mayors over the next two years.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Healey’s first budget to include big devolution package to boost growth

articles.author: Priya Bharadia
articles.description:
Fender criticises stadium pricing, calling it ‘bollocks’ and says it ‘won’t be happening’ on his tour
Sam Fender has responded to criticism by fans about ticket prices for his 2027 stadium tour by promising he would lower the cost, telling followers on Instagram: “They’re getting changed.”
The 32-year-old musician announced his Proper Massive stadium tour earlier this week.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Sam Fender tells fans high ticket prices for Proper Massive tour are ‘getting changed’

articles.author: Priya Bharadia
articles.description:
Second named storm will hit northern parts of UK as thousands remain without power after Friday’s Storm Austen
The UK is bracing for a second storm this weekend, as strong winds and heavy rain are expected to disrupt travel and cause further power cuts in the north.
Storm Boelo, the second named storm of the season, is expected to bring heavy, frequent showers and winds potentially exceeding 80mph to northern parts of the UK.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Storm Boelo to bring 80mph gusts and heavy rain to parts of UK

articles.author: Tara Conlan
articles.description:
BBC series deliberately uses ‘more organic’ shots to assure viewers animals are not AI-generated, producers say
The David Attenborough-narrated series Blue Planet III deliberately includes cloudier, less polished footage to counter AI fakery and assure viewers it is “authentic”, its producers have said.
Nearly a decade after Blue Planet II shone a light on plastic pollution, and 25 years since the first Blue Planet aired, the hit BBC series is returning with more animal behaviour and cutting-edge technology, including the world’s first underwater CCTV camera – dubbed “stonefish” cam.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Blue Planet III features cloudier footage to prove authenticity amid AI boom

articles.author: Patrick Barkham
articles.description:
Tim and Geli Harris have spent more than a decade fighting to protect Catfield Fen, a rare wetland in the Norfolk Broads
Polluters and regulators who fail to stop pollution must quake in their boots when they receive a letter from the lawyers for Tim and Geli Harris. The couple, who farm 460 acres in the Norfolk Broads, have now scored a hat-trick of landmark legal victories to save an internationally important wetland after they won again in the high court this month.
Lady Justice Lieven found that Natural England failed in its statutory duty to protect Catfield Fen from pollution after nitrates and phosphates washed from arable fields into one of the finest examples of calcareous fen in western Europe, home to 2,500 species including rarities such as the fen orchid, crested buckler fern, breeding bittern and swallowtail butterflies.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘You need persistence’: the Norfolk couple who took on environmental regulators three times – and won

articles.author: Presented by Aditya Chakrabortty, produced by Frankie Tobi and Luke John Smith; the executive producers are Maz Ebtehaj, Kirsty Major and James Tindale
articles.description:
Are we doomscrolling our way into a democratic crisis? That’s what the playwright James Graham fears may be happening, as he suggests that our algorithms have led us into ‘a massive crisis of the new’ and are preventing us from imagining a different future
Watch the full episode with James Graham here.
 

 

 INK will be released in UK cinemas on 8 January 2027
Aditya suggested reading (and watching) list for James Graham:
Dear England: about England’s football team
Sherwood: mentioned in the conversation, set in the village where James Graham grew up in the shadow of the miners’ strike
Quiz: set on the British quiz show, Who wants to be a millionaire, where a contestant wins a million quid
 Continue reading...
articles.title: “Culture is stagnant, so politics is stuck” – playwright James Graham | Radical Thinking – podcast

articles.author: Sarah Butler
articles.description:
Closures within chain formerly under the WH Smith brand raise fears of high streets becoming ‘postal deserts’
Towns and even city centres face being left as “postal deserts” after it emerged that more than a third of post offices within the troubled TG Jones chain are closing.
So far this year 36 branches within the high street chain formerly known as WH Smith have closed and a further 34 are set to close by early 2027, according to Post Office records analysed by the Guardian.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: More than third of post offices in TG Jones stores to shut by early 2027

articles.author: Helena Horton
articles.description:
Historic England archaeologist says some inns’ claims to date back 1,000 years are inaccurate and oldest is from 1430
With their low ceilings, timber beams and roaring fires, many of England’s inns lay claim to being the oldest in the land and to have been visited by Vikings and Saxons.
But an archaeologist who worked on behalf of Historic England says not one of the more than two dozen pubs that make this claim is being accurate.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Which is really England’s oldest pub? Tree-ring dating helps settle debate

articles.author: Caroline Davies
articles.description:
Duchess of Sussex’s decision to cut ties with elderly father cast in new light as he faces sexual abuse image claims

Meghan ‘deeply distressed’ by allegations against father

The depiction of the Duchess of Sussex by certain sections of the media has often been one of a fame-hungry daughter casting off an elderly father in his declining years and keeping him from his grandchildren as she embraces the international celebrity stage.
Their estrangement has been the subject of countless headlines since her marriage to Prince Harry. But her statement today, released after child sexual abuse image allegations made against Thomas Markle Sr, 82, suggests deeper, darker fears as the cause.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Allegations against Thomas Markle Sr challenge media’s Meghan narrative

articles.author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
articles.description:
Exclusive: Angela Eagle tells utility bosses next price review ‘must focus on value for money for customers’
Ministers will make an unprecedented intervention in water bills and how companies prioritise investment, directing bosses to bring down costs and stop leaks and sewage overflows.
Angela Eagle, the environment secretary, has told suppliers in England and Wales she plans to intervene in the next price review – conducted by the water regulator, Ofwat.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK government to make unprecedented intervention in setting of water bills

articles.author: Mark Sweney
articles.description:
World’s second largest brewer says use of drugs such as Wegovy can reduce desire to drink alcohol
Heineken has warned British bars and pubs that the boom in popularity of weight-loss drugs could lead to a fall in sales of beer and cider.
The world’s second-largest brewer sent a presentation to British hospitality customers earlier this month that said the use of GLP-1 medication – such as Ozempic and Wegovy – could reduce the desire to drink alcohol. This in turn could result in “fullness and fewer serves” of pints in pubs and bars, it added.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Boom in weight-loss drugs could lead to fall in beer sales, Heineken warns UK pubs

articles.author: Megan Davies, Claire Jones and Magdalena Shopova for MetDesk
articles.description:
Storm Adam brings torrential rain to Valencia, Alicante and Balearic Islands, as Storm Austen strikes England and Wales
Storm Adam brought torrential rain to eastern Spain earlier this week. In Pego, Alicante, 632mm fell in 36 hours, with 430mm of this falling in just six hours, while the Valencian town of Olivia received 600mm in 24 hours.
The severe flooding led 145 municipalities across Valencia and Alicante to impose a temporary lockdown on about 850,000 people on Monday. At least five people have died, 500 have been rescued and 2,100 evacuated.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Severe flooding in eastern Spain and UK hit by first named storm of winter

articles.author: Ajit Niranjan
articles.description:
People succumbed to heat at highest rates in Malta, Italy and Hungary, with health issues, loneliness and poverty exacerbating toll
Heat killed a record 50,000 people in European cities this summer, new research suggests, with scientists blaming climate breakdown for two in every three of the deaths.
